summary: The nansen-trading skill drives the Nansen CLI (`nansen trade`, `nansen perp`) to quote and execute Solana/Base DEX swaps, cross-chain bridges, Solana limit orders and Hyperliquid perp trades, all of which are irreversible on-chain. It needs the `nansen` binary (installed from the npm package nansen-cli), a NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD that it tells the agent to persist in plaintext at ~/.nansen/.env, a NANSEN_API_KEY or browser session, and a Nansen-managed wallet. It talks to the Nansen API (compliance screening, price lookup, quotes), Hyperliquid and RPC endpoints. Only NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD is declared in requires.env; NANSEN_API_KEY is declared only as primaryEnv, and NANSEN_YES and NANSEN_REQUIRE_CONFIRM are not declared at all.

findings.message: The wallet encryption password NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD is persisted in ~/.nansen/.env and sourced before every trade execute, so a wallet credential sits in plaintext on disk.
The agent is told to generate and persist a wallet password via the nansen-wallet-manager skill if one is missing, so it creates and stores a wallet credential itself.
The skill requires `nansen wallet create`; the wallet holds both EVM and Solana keys and is used to sign irreversible trades.
NANSEN_API_KEY is declared only as primaryEnv and not in requires.env, although the skill depends on it for authentication.
NANSEN_YES and NANSEN_REQUIRE_CONFIRM are used to control confirmation behavior but are not declared in requires.env.
Non-interactive agent runs broadcast irreversible trades without any prompt unless the operator sets NANSEN_REQUIRE_CONFIRM=1, and --yes is a no-op there.
The skill installs the npm package nansen-cli, which provides the nansen binary, and grants allowed-tools Bash(nansen:*).
Wallet addresses are sent to the Nansen API for compliance screening before quote and execute, and the API key or session is sent to the Nansen API.
Perp commands query and submit signed orders to Hyperliquid.
The skill card itself says ClawScan marked the skill suspicious (the scan was partial) for saving a wallet password in a plaintext .env file.
